sections.title: Life cycle and habitat
sections.text: Bull thistle is a biennial native to Eurasia and north-western Africa and introduced elsewhere. In its first year it forms a rosette and taproot; the flowering stem, winged and spiny, can reach about 2 m. It colonises pastures, rough ground and other disturbed soils.

sections.title: Flower heads and fruits
sections.text: Its purple flower heads are about 2.5–5 cm across and the achenes bear a feathery pappus. The plate matches the prickly leaves, winged stem, involucres and plumed fruits. No food use is established here.
